disease_label_per_paper: Salmonella renal abscess in an immunocompetent child
presentation_summary: 10-year-old girl with no significant past medical history presented with one week of fever and intermittent vomiting, plus one day of abdominal pain and localized discomfort over the left hypochondrium.

Two weeks earlier she had four days of fever with diarrhea and vomiting that resolved spontaneously; there was no recent trauma, sick contact, or travel, except a superficial household-cat scratch three months before.
On admission she was alert and non-toxic, febrile to 38.5 C, had left costovertebral angle tenderness, and denied dysuria or urinary frequency.

Admission labs showed WBC 18.23 x 10^9/L, absolute neutrophils 10.03 x 10^9/L, CRP 62.5 mg/L, ESR 74 mm/hr, serum urea 3.1 mmol/L, creatinine 36 umol/L, sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 3.8 mmol/L, bicarbonate 23 mmol/L, chloride 103 mmol/L.
Urinalysis was largely unremarkable: specific gravity 1.005, RBC 0/uL, WBC 0/uL, protein 1+, nitrite nil, leukocyte nil, glucose nil, casts nil, crystals nil; urine culture had no growth.
Renal ultrasound on admission day two showed multiple kidney cysts and a 4.2 x 4.0 x 3.1 cm heterogeneous liquefied structure from the left mid to lower pole, consistent with renal abscess.

microbiology.result: Group C Salmonella species, serotyped as Salmonella serovar Oranienburg; susceptible to ampicillin, ceftriaxone, and co-trimoxazole

procedures.source_text_value: 15 mL of brown frank pus was aspirated and the drain was left in situ

clinical_course.event: IV gentamicin 5 mg/kg/day was initiated for concern of pyelonephritis.
After renal abscess was detected, therapy was switched to IV ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg/day for better abscess penetration and image-guided drainage was performed.
Fever lysed by the second day post-drainage.
Ultrasound day 3 post-drainage showed abscess decreased to 2.0 x 1.9 x 1.9 cm.
CRP normalized by day 10 post-drainage to 4.1 mg/L; abscess decreased to 2.1 x 1.4 x 1.6 cm and the drain was removed.
Discharged after two weeks IV ceftriaxone with four further weeks of oral co-trimoxazole.
By day 27 post-drainage the abscess had resolved completely on ultrasound.

actual_treatment: IV ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg/day after abscess detection

quality_warnings: Salmonella serotype, susceptibility, drainage fluid culture, immunologic screen, serial ultrasound response, and cure are retained with use_in_ranking=false.
Absence of pyuria and urinary symptoms is encoded in presentation observations because it is presentation-time evidence and should not be deleted to force a urinary-source pattern.
Multiple kidney cysts are retained in imaging text and risk context but not used as a hard diagnosis or final source label.
